title: Scanning a windowed configuration encoding
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine, let $x$ be a Boolean input, let $s$ be a natural number, and let $C$ be a configuration of $N$ on input $x$. Suppose every work-tape head of $C$ lies within distance $s$ of the origin and every work-tape cell outside that window is blank. Scan the initial $W(2s+1)$ bits of the encoded configuration word by the virtual scanner. Its recorded head and output summary is exactly the configuration's state and output summary; the scanner's acceptance condition holds, its recorded work-tape symbols at each tape head agree with $C$, and its blankness flag is true exactly when every window cell has the specified joint-blank property.
hypotheses_covered: N is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine
C is a configuration of N on input x
Every work-tape head position has absolute value at most s
Every work-tape cell outside the window has no symbol
caveat: Several scanner-state fields and the cell blankness predicate are specified only through tuple projections and definitions, so their full encoding-level meaning cannot be expanded from the supplied informal definitions.
